title: Ops Engineer Momentum Mini-Deck (rough)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, operator-first snack deck to accelerate pilots with platform & infra teams (SRE / infra / platform engineering). Aim: 3 minutes to explain value, 7 minutes to land technical credibility, and a repeatable pilot script that reduces friction for the first week. Draft/working — meant for SEs to adapt on calls and for internal review.

Slide 1 — One-sentence lead + problem framing
- Lead: "Make inference predictable for production apps — without building the entire serving stack."
- Problem bullets (ops POV):
  - Burden: model serving complexity — autoscaling, KV caches, custom kernels.
  - Unpredictable unit economics across traffic shapes.
  - Fallback and multi-variant routing gaps during incidents.
- Why they should care: reliability incidents + cost spikes = product slowdown.

Slide 2 — Redwood technical narrative (operator-first)
- Runtime: GPU-optimized serving with continuous batching and KV cache warming.
- Routing: policy-layer for latency vs cost with automatic fallbacks to compatible variants.
- Observability: token-level latency traces, per-route heatmaps, and end-to-end fallthrough logs.
- Ops levers exposed: batching policy, cache TTLs, reserved burst capacity, and rollback strategies.

Slide 3 — Proof points (concise)
- Internal benchmark: 35% token-cost drop for bursty customer X using prefix caching + batching.
- SLO story: configurable p99 SLO, automatic fallback to lower-capacity variants on sustained overload.
- Compatibility: integrates with existing KMS, VPC peering options, and on-prem private control plane.

Slide 4 — Pilot proposal (7–14 day quick pilot)
- Goal: validate latency, regression-free quality, and cost per 100k active monthly users.
- Core steps:
  1) Authenticate + smoke test (2 hours): API key, test route, simple generation.
  2) Canary (day 1–2): route 1–5% traffic through Redwood dedicated/reserved pool.
  3) Observability validation (day 2–4): ensure token-level metrics, tracing hooks, and cost dashboards are visible to the team.
  4) Failure-injection (day 4–6): simulate model or zone failure — observe fallback and latency impact.
  5) Scale test (day 7–10): synthetic load ramp to predicted day-peak QPS.
  6) Wrap & decision (day 11–14): handoff checklist, suggested commitment levels (if any).
- Success criteria (example): p50 latency within 10% of baseline, p99 <= agreed SLO, no more than 3% request error rate during ramp, <10% increase in developer latency for tokenized flows.

Slide 5 — Canaries and fallback mechanics (quick tech details for SRE)
- Routing policy primitives: region, capacity tier, cost-tier, model-variant compatibility.
- Fallback sentinel: health-check + progressive degrade (full model -> quantized variant -> cached responses -> stub response).
- KV/cache warming: recommended warm-up traffic pattern + TTL settings.

Slide 6 — Battlecard: top objections & rapid responses (ops-focused)
- Objection: "We host our own models — why use Redwood?"
  - Response: "Redwood reduces ops lift (batching, kernel selection, KV cache) and provides a predictable economic layer while letting you keep private deployments via Redwood Private. Think: keep models, offload serving."
- Objection: "Latency spikes are unacceptable."
  - Response: "We expose per-token traces, burst pools, and routing fallbacks. Standard pilot includes failure-injection testing so you can validate p99 under realistic outages."
- Objection: "Vendor lock-in / portability risk."
  - Response: "Model pinning and standard model artifacts + can export logs & KV snapshot; private mode keeps control plane in your VPC."
- Objection: "Cost — how do you compare to self-host?"
  - Response: "We provide comparative unit-economics reports during pilot (token cost, ops hours saved). For many bursty workloads, caching + batching reduces net cost vs naive self-hosting."
- Quick tip: always offer an A/B run comparison for 1 week vs incumbent to make cost argument tangible.

Slide 7 — Demo script for SEs (8–12 minutes)
- 90s pitch, 3-step live demo:
  1) Smoke call: single request, streaming response to show latency & functions.
  2) Trace demo: show token-level flamegraph and explain cost breakdown.
  3) Failover: flip region/policy and show transparent fallback to a compatible variant.
- Data to capture live: p50/p95/p99, tokens/req, error rate, cache hit rate.

Appendix — Pilot checklist (copyable for AE/SE)
- Pre-call: gather baseline metrics (current p50/p95/p99, cost per 100k tokens, average request length).
- Access: API key, VPC peering info (if private), KMS ARN (if needed).
- Configs to prepare: route + policy JSON, initial model variant, batching target ms, cache TTL.
- Logging: ensure your observability team has read-only dashboard link.
- Rollback plan: instant route disable + canned SRE runbook (included in pilot artifact).

Rapid integrations & tips (ops notes)
- Typical knob starting points: batching target = 25–40ms, cache TTL = 60s for conversational prefixes, reserved burst = 20% of peak QPS for pilot.
- Quantization recommendation: test 8-bit variant for throughput-bound workloads; validate with 100 synthetic queries for quality drift.
- Prefix caching pattern: identify top 20% prefixes by volume and seed KV before ramp.

Linked artifacts & handoffs
- Include links in pilot folder: pilot-runbook.md, dashboard snapshot, cost-comparison-csv, failure-injection-scripts.
- Suggested follow-up: 1-week sync + runbook sign-off or escalate to dedicated contract repricing.

Open questions & TODOs (internal)
- Add a short case snippet from a customer that measured cost drop from prefix caching (ask Analytics for anonymized numbers).
- Build quick A/B script that automates 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% increments for SEs.
- Confirm default suggested batching TTLs with runtime team.

Speaker notes (short):
- Frame conversation around ops risk first, features second.
- Always ask: "How do you measure a bad inference incident today?" — anchor SLO conversation there.
- End every pilot offer with a concrete decision date and a one-page handoff.

Quick file exports to create for pilot folder:
- pilot-runbook.md (detailed step-by-step)
- pilot-dashboard-link.txt (readonly Grafana link)
- cost-assumptions.csv (tokens, avg len, price tiers)
- failure-injection/README.md (how to run)

Notes to SEs (rapid copy-paste lines):
- "We'll do a 7–14 day pilot: can we pick a decision date now?"
- "We'll show you per-token latency and a cost comparison for the same traffic shape — you'll get the CSV in 48 hours."

End of mini-deck.

Notes: this doc is intentionally concise — use it as a live script and expand into an SE-specific slide deck (8 slides max) for calls. Replace any example metrics with the customer's real baselines during prep.
